question.problem:
Let $V=C[0,\frac{\pi }{2}],$ the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,\frac{\pi }{2}].$ Find $⟨t,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩$ if the inner product on $V$ is defined as

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$
question.worked_solution:
We need to evaluate

$$
⟨t,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t.
$$

Let's use integration by parts. We denote

$$
\begin{aligned}u=t & ⟹ & {u}^{′}=1, \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡t & ⟹ & v=\int {v}^{′}\,\text{d}t=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t=\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting into the formula for the integration by parts, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t & =uv{|}_{0}^{\pi /2}-{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}t \\  & =(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t){|}_{0}^{\pi /2}-{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =(\frac{\pi }{2}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{2}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡0)+\operatorname{cos}⁡t{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}+(\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}-\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}-1.\end{aligned}
$$
